How to Access Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 (Updated September 2026)

Short answer: Claude Fable 5 is available again. Anthropic restored it July 1, 2026 after an 18-day export-control suspension. Use it on paid Claude plans, Claude Code or the API (claude-fable-5). Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1) launched September 1 at the same $10/$50 price. Mythos 5 is limited to approved partners.

Status checked September 26, 2026 against Anthropic's Fable 5.1 announcement, the redeployment notice, the Claude Platform pricing page and the Fable 5 model docs. Anthropic still lists the original Fable 5 (claude-fable-5) on its pricing page, but recommends 5.1 as the current model. Everything below covers Fable 5, with the 5.1 differences called out. See what changed in Fable 5.1 and Fable 5.1 pricing and benchmarks for the newer model.
Is Claude Fable 5 available right now?
Yes, with three things to know:

June 12 suspension. The US government applied export controls to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 on June 12, 2026. Anthropic had no reliable way to verify nationality in real time, so it suspended access for everyone. It lifted the suspension on June 30 and access resumed July 1. The full story is in our government shutdown breakdown.

Plans. Fable is not on the free plan. Anthropic's pricing page lists Fable 5.1 for Pro, Max and Team through usage credits, with 50% of weekly limits, and includes it for Enterprise. Plan terms changed several times after launch (a July 18 announcement, reported by Dawn, kept it on Max and Team Premium at 50% of limits and moved Pro and Team Standard to usage credits), so check claude.com/pricing before you count on it.
API. Developers can call claude-fable-5 or claude-fable-5-1. Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry also list Fable 5.

You can reach Claude Fable 5 through 4 routes: pick it from the model dropdown on claude.ai with a paid plan, run it in Claude Code with claude --model claude-fable-5, select it in the desktop app under Model preferences, or call model ID claude-fable-5 on the Anthropic API.

Anthropic shipped Fable 5 on June 8, 2026 (Anthropic's docs list API availability from June 9) as the first publicly released model in the new Mythos-class family. Independent testing from Every's team puts it at 91/100 on the Senior Engineer benchmark, next to Opus 4.8's 63 and GPT-5.5's 62. Anthropic calls it the most capable model it has ever made available to the public.

This guide walks through each access path in detail: Claude.ai, Claude Code, the desktop app, and the Anthropic API. It also covers the difference between Fable 5 (the consumer release) and Mythos 5 (the limited-access variant without safeguards), real pricing, and where Fable beats or wastes your money. If you would rather skip Fable, our Claude Fable 5 alternatives list what else to run.

What Is Claude Fable 5?

Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's June 2026 flagship model. It's the first public release of the "Mythos-class" architecture, a class of models Anthropic restricted in April when an earlier Mythos version was deemed too risky to release without guardrails. After months of red-teaming and partner feedback, Anthropic shipped Fable 5 as the public-safe variant: the same base model with safety classifiers that can decline certain requests. Anthropic's docs describe refusals as a stop_reason: "refusal" response, and a declined request can be retried on another Claude model through a fallback.
Three things make Fable 5 different from Opus 4.8 or Sonnet 5:

End-to-end task ownership. Fable 5 is built for long, async assignments: multi-hour runs where it plans, uses tools, repairs its own output, and ships a finished result. It's not designed for the back-and-forth rhythm of a chat.

Code quality at the senior level. On Every's Senior Engineer benchmark, Fable 5 scored 91/100, near the range of human senior engineers who've taken the same test. Opus 4.8 scored 63; GPT-5.5 scored 62.

One-shot complex builds. In day-one testing, the Every team built a custom transcription app, a pixel-perfect 3D rendering of Borges's Library of Babel, and a strategic conversion-optimization report, each from a single prompt.
Fable 5 vs Mythos 5: which one are you actually getting?
This is the part most coverage glosses over. There are two models in the Mythos-class release:
Anthropic says customers without Mythos access can use Fable, which needs no approval and offers the same capabilities.

If you specifically want Mythos-class access today: Mythos 5 is offered through Project Glasswing. Its successor, Mythos 5.1, is gated through two named, concrete programs instead: Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program for vetted cybersecurity organizations, and the Life Sciences Verification Program, run in partnership with the US government, for vetted life-sciences organizations. Neither is a public sign-up; both require an organization to apply and be vetted.

How to Access Claude Fable 5 (4 Paths)
Fable 5 is available across four surfaces: the Claude web app, Claude Code, the desktop app, and the Anthropic API. Each one has trade-offs.
1. Claude.ai (Web App)
The fastest way to try Fable 5 with zero setup.
Steps:
Go to claude.ai and sign in to a paid Claude plan (Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise).

Open a new chat. The model picker lists the current Fable model (Fable 5.1 as of September 2026) next to the other Claude models. Fable is metered through usage credits on some plans, see the status section above.
Select the Fable model from the dropdown.
Start prompting.

When this is the right surface: quick one-shot prompts where you want to read the output in the browser. Good for prototyping a single artifact (a web app, a research report, a code module) without setting up tooling.
Limitations: no local file access, no shell execution, no long async runs. Fable draws on your plan's Fable allowance or usage credits, which a long run can burn through quickly.
2. Claude Code (CLI)

Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-based coding agent. Fable 5 inside Claude Code is the most powerful way to use the model for engineering work, because it can plan, edit files, run tests, debug failures, and iterate over multi-hour runs.
Steps:
Install or update Claude Code: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code # or update an existing install: claude update
Start claude in your project and sign in when prompted (skip this if you already have).

Set Fable 5 as the active model for a session: claude --model claude-fable-5 For the newer model, use claude --model claude-fable-5-1. Or use the in-CLI /model command after launching: /model claude-fable-5
Start a session in your project root and give it a complete task. Fable 5 is designed to own the whole assignment.

When this is the right surface: large engineering tasks (build a feature end-to-end, refactor a module, port a library, write an integration with tests). Match Fable 5's design intent: long async runs with a fully framed brief.

Pricing note inside Claude Code: Fable use in Claude Code counts against your plan's Fable allowance or usage credits, and API-key use bills at $10/M input and $50/M output. Heavy use will eat into your limit fast. If you're running Claude Code in production, our Claude Code security audit locks down what the agent can access before it touches sensitive code.
3. Claude Desktop App
The desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) gives you Claude.ai's chat experience plus local file integrations (artifacts, attachments) and a faster keyboard-first flow than the web.
Steps:
Download the latest Claude desktop app from claude.ai/download.
Sign in with your Claude account.
Open settings → Model preferences → select the Fable model.
Start a chat. The desktop app supports drag-and-drop file attachments and a system tray quick-prompt.
When this is the right surface: writing, document analysis, research synthesis. Anywhere you want chat polish plus local file access but don't need shell execution.
4. Anthropic API
For programmatic access (building a product, an agent, a batch pipeline) the API is the only path.

Model IDs: claude-fable-5 for the original and claude-fable-5-1 for Fable 5.1, per Anthropic's model docs. Both have a 1M token context window by default and up to 128k output tokens per request (Fable 5 docs).

API-only features worth knowing:
Prompt caching is supported and matters for multi-step agents. Cache reads cost $1 per million tokens on Fable 5 and $0.25 on Fable 5.1.
Thinking is always on and raw reasoning is never returned. Control depth with the effort parameter.
A request the safety classifiers decline returns stop_reason: "refusal" with HTTP 200. Since September 24, 2026, some refusals that arrive before any output are billed, per Anthropic's docs.
Streaming is supported. Use it; Fable 5 runs are slow, and streaming gives you progress visibility instead of a 90-second blank wait.
Claude Fable 5 Pricing (and Why It Matters)

Prices from Anthropic's pricing page, checked September 26, 2026. Sonnet 5's $2/$10 began as introductory pricing and Anthropic now lists it as the standard price. Batch requests are half price ($5/$25 for Fable). Fable 5 costs 2x Opus 4.8 and 5x Sonnet 5 per token. Add Fable's slower runs and heavier token use on complex tasks, and one long session can cost several times what the same task costs on Sonnet.

The practical implication: don't reach for Fable 5 by default. Save it for jobs where you'd otherwise hire a senior engineer for a half-day. For everything else, Sonnet 5 or Opus 4.8 is the right call. For the full cost-per-workload breakdown, see our Fable 5 pricing guide.
When to Use Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8 vs Sonnet 5

The headline rule from Every's day-zero review: Fable 5 rewards a sharp problem frame and a strong review process. If you can't define the whole assignment before you hit send, you'll waste tokens on a model that isn't optimized for clarification rounds.
How to Get the Best Results from Fable 5
Three patterns from the first week of public use:
1. Treat it as an async agent, not a chat partner

Fable 5's design intent is "give it a complete task, walk away for 30-90 minutes, come back and review." The worst way to use it is to send a vague prompt and try to steer it interactively. The best way is to frame the whole assignment up front:
Problem statement (one paragraph)
Constraints (what NOT to do)
Examples of the shape of the answer you want
Success criteria (how you'll judge the output)

Send that, let it run, and review carefully. If you'd rather have a team build and maintain agent workflows like this for you instead of managing the framing and review yourself, our AI agent development service handles the setup, tooling, and ongoing maintenance end-to-end.
2. Run several jobs in parallel

Because each Fable 5 run is slow, the rate-limiter is your review capacity, not the model. Kick off three or four independent runs at once on different problems. By the time you finish reviewing the first output, the others are done.
3. Invest in the framing, not the iteration

Most chat-style prompt engineering tips don't apply. You're not refining over 10 turns; you're writing one well-framed brief and reading one detailed output. The skill that matters is the same skill that makes you good at delegating to a senior contractor: write a tight, testable brief.
Common Setup Issues (and Fixes)

"Claude Fable 5" isn't in my model picker on Claude.ai You're either on the free plan (Fable is not included) or your plan needs usage credits enabled for Fable. Sign in to a paid plan, check your usage-credit settings and reload.
Claude Code says "model not found" for claude-fable-5 Your CLI is out of date. Run claude update or reinstall via npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code.
API returns 404 on model: "claude-fable-5" Two possibilities:
Your API key is on an organization that hasn't been migrated to the new model yet. Check the models endpoint for the exact model ID your org sees.
You're hitting an older API version. Make sure your client SDK is on the latest @anthropic-ai/sdk (Node) or anthropic (Python).

Fable 5 declines my request Fable's safety classifiers can decline some requests, and the API returns stop_reason: "refusal". Retry on another Claude model or use the fallbacks parameter described in Anthropic's refusals and fallback docs. For legitimate security or life-sciences work, Mythos access goes through Anthropic's Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program (Mythos 5.1) or Project Glasswing.

I'm hitting usage limits within hours Fable 5 is token-hungry on complex tasks. A long engineering run can consume a lot of tokens (we have not measured a typical figure). Check your usage and credit balance on the Claude billing page and consider Max or Team if you run Fable jobs daily.
What You Can Actually Build (Day-One Examples)
From Every's published day-zero test (seven testers, one week of use, single prompts each):
Custom transcription app: a web app that brightens and levels grainy audio lectures, transcribes them, and lights up each sentence as the speaker says it. Built and deployed in one prompt.
3D Library of Babel: pixel-perfect rendering of Borges's hexagonal-room infinite library, fully navigable in browser. Single prompt.
PULSE Browser Studio: a browser-based creative tool. Single prompt.

Strategic conversion-optimization report: synthesized hundreds of survey responses + an entire web analytics stack, identified the biggest conversion issue, and proposed a clean falsifiable experiment.
The common pattern: a single well-framed brief and a single run that returns a finished artifact. Not "iterate over twenty turns until it works."

Should You Switch from Opus 4.8 to Fable 5?

For most developers, honestly, no. Not as a default. The right move is to keep Opus 4.8 (or Sonnet 5) as your everyday driver and reach for Fable 5 deliberately when you have a long, async-friendly assignment with real complexity. We break the choice down task-by-task in our Fable 5 vs Opus 4.8 comparison.

The cost math is brutal if you misuse it: Fable 5 at $50/M output tokens on a multi-hour run can cost $5-$20 per session. That's fine when the output is worth a half-day of senior engineering time. It's wasteful when you're asking a quick question.

The Every team's verdict, "a warp drive for power users, overpowered for everyone else," is a fair summary. If you're already at the top of the AI adoption curve (using Claude Code in production, building agents, delegating real work), Fable 5 will open up new categories of task. If you're earlier on that curve, you'll struggle to find tasks that justify the wait and the spend.
FAQ
Is there a Claude Fable 5 app or APK to download?

No. Claude Fable 5 is not a standalone app or APK; it's a model you select inside an existing Claude surface. There are only two things you actually download: the Claude desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) from claude.ai/download, or the Claude Code CLI via npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code. Either way, you pick "Claude Fable 5" from the model list once you're signed in, you don't download the model itself.
Is Claude Fable 5 free?

No. Anthropic's pricing page lists Fable as not included on the free plan. It is available on paid plans through usage credits or plan allowances, or through a metered Anthropic API key at $10/$50 per million tokens. If you want a free option while you wait or want to avoid the cost, see the free AI models you can use instead.
How do I access Claude Mythos 5 specifically?

You can't, unless Anthropic approves your organization. Mythos 5 has the same capabilities as Fable 5 without the safety classifiers and is offered through Project Glasswing; contact your Anthropic, AWS or Google Cloud account team. Mythos 5.1 goes to vetted organizations in the Cyber Verification Program or Life Sciences Verification Program. For 99% of developers, Fable 5 (the public, safeguarded release) is the version you're actually looking for.
What's the fastest way to start using Fable 5?

Sign in to a paid Claude plan at claude.ai, open a new chat, and pick the Fable model in the model picker. That's the zero-setup path. For engineering work, install or update Claude Code (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code) and run claude --model claude-fable-5 for the full agentic experience instead of just chat.
Why can't I find Claude Fable 5 in my model picker?

Most likely you're on the free plan, where Fable is not included, or your paid plan needs usage credits turned on for Fable. In Claude Code, an outdated CLI causes a "model not found" error; run claude update to fix it.
Is Claude Fable 5 still available after the June 12 suspension?

Yes. The US government's export controls on Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were lifted on June 30, 2026, and access resumed July 1 on Claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude Platform. Anthropic's pricing page still lists Fable 5 next to Fable 5.1. Read the full shutdown timeline.
What is the difference between Claude Fable 5 and Fable 5.1?

Fable 5.1 shipped September 1, 2026 with model ID claude-fable-5-1. Input and output prices match Fable 5 ($10 and $50 per million tokens), but cache reads drop from $1 to $0.25 per million. Anthropic says that cuts typical workload costs about 25%. Details in our Fable 5.1 breakdown.
How much does Claude Fable 5 cost?

The API price is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, half that on the Batch API. On Claude plans, Fable runs through usage credits or a plan allowance depending on your tier. Our Fable 5 pricing guide works through cost per workload.
Bottom Line: Action Plan
If you want to use Fable 5 today, here's the shortest path:
Sign in to your paid Claude plan at claude.ai and verify Fable is in your model picker.
Update Claude Code with claude update or a fresh npm install.
Pick one big, well-framed task that's been sitting in your backlog because it would take half a day of senior engineering. Write a complete brief.
Run it on Fable via Claude Code (claude --model claude-fable-5) and walk away.
Review carefully when it finishes. The model's ceiling is high, but the responsibility for judging quality stays with you.
For everything else, keep Sonnet 5 or Opus 4.8 on hand. Match the model to the assignment.
Working with Claude Fable 5 in Production?

If you're shipping AI features into production (agents, multi-step pipelines, Claude Code workflows), Fable 5's pricing and pace make engineering judgment more valuable, not less. The teams that get the most out of it pair the model with senior AI engineers who know how to frame the assignment and review the output.
